# V1.7.0 — running ledger of code changes

**Charter (set 2026-07-23):** the active running batch — successor to [v1.6.9.md](v1.6.9.md) (released to closed testing 2026-07-23). Same rule as every version doc — the running catch-all for every code change we accumulate, big or small, until it is built and committed. ## Item 1 — Seed testdev7/testdev8 with a full realistic data profile (Play Store screenshot candidates)

- **Status:** ✅ **DONE 2026-07-23** (Sonnet, medium effort — data population following established schema/entity patterns, not new architecture; the effort was in volume/internal-consistency across ~2 months of data for a paired couple). **Grilled first** to pin down both personas (income, accounts, goals, bills, spend shape), then written directly into the staging Supabase DB via the read-write MCP (`mcp__supabase__execute_sql`), respecting ADR-0001 (LWW `updated_at`/`server_rev`, both handled automatically — `server_rev` is trigger-assigned, `updated_at` defaults `now()` on insert), ADR-0002 (no local `pending_sync` involved — these are server-native rows, the app just needs a pull-sync to bring them into Room), ADR-0007 (balance derived — only `opening_balance` + ledger rows were written, current balance was never touched directly), ADR-0009 (inserted in FK order: accounts → categories → recurring_rules → transactions → savings_goals/goal_contributions), and ADR-0049 (`exclude_from_analysis` on the reimbursable pair). No schema/Room change — reused existing tables only.
- **Request:** Alvin — candidate couple for the eventual Play Store screenshot re-render ([deferred Item 41](deferred.md#item-41--play-store-screenshot-refresh-playful-pop-reskin), still held for the final shipping UI) is **testdev7 + testdev8** (confirmed actively paired 2026-07-04, `couple_id 82dba413-bb5b-4488-93c5-5af5431ffba2`). Wants both accounts fully populated — accounts (incl. savings), recurring bills, recurring salaries, reimbursables, and transactions spanning **June 2026–present** — so the screenshots show a lived-in app, not empty/sparse test data. Explicitly asked to profile the two personas in a grilling session before populating, and confirmed mid-build that population should happen now, not just be documented as a plan.
- **Relationship to Item 41:** data-prep only, not the screenshot capture/render pipeline itself (still correctly deferred until the reskin settles). Populating testdev7/8 now is independent prep that isn't blocked by that gate.
- **Grilled persona (locked 2026-07-23):**
  - **Juan (testdev7, accent `#1565C0`)** — salaried, ₱45,000/mo, paid **semi-monthly on the 15th & 30th** (₱22,500/cut) to his Bank account. Fronts occasional work expenses (Reimbursable/Reimbursement category pair, ADR-0049, excluded from Analysis).
  - **Maria (testdev8, accent `#C62828`)** — salaried, ₱32,000/mo, paid **semi-monthly on the 10th & 25th** (₱16,000/cut) to her Bank account.
  - **Accounts** (starter Cash/GCash/Bank Account kept per person, plus): a personal **Credit Card** each, and a couple-owned **Joint Bank** account (ADR-0018, `couple_id` set, created by Juan) carrying the shared rent/utilities.
  - **Opening balances** (as of 2026-06-01, before the seeded ledger): Juan — Cash ₱2,500 · GCash ₱4,000 · Bank ₱35,000 · Credit Card ₱0. Maria — Cash ₱1,800 · GCash ₱3,200 · Bank ₱22,000 · Credit Card ₱0. Joint Bank ₱15,000.
  - **Savings goals** (`savings_goals`/`goal_contributions`, monthly-lump cadence): shared **"Baguio Trip"** (target ₱80,000, due Dec 2026) — ₱17,000 from Juan in June + ₱17,000 from Maria in July → ₱34,000 (42.5%); Juan's personal **"New Laptop"** (₱65,000, due Oct 2026) — ₱9,000 × 2 → ₱18,000 (27.7%); Maria's personal **"Emergency Fund"** (₱50,000, no due date) — ₱16,000 × 2 → ₱32,000 (64%).
  - **Recurring bills** (`recurring_rules`, `auto_post=false` — confirm-on-arrival per ADR-0048, all owned by the payer): Joint account — Rent ₱18,000 (1st), Electricity ₱3,500 (5th), Water ₱800 (5th), Internet ₱2,000 (10th), all owned by Juan. Juan's Bank — Netflix ₱549 (15th), Spotify ₱149 (20th). Maria's Bank — Phone plan ₱1,299 (25th), Gym membership ₱1,500 (1st). Every rule's `next_date` was set to its true next occurrence **after** 2026-07-23 (Aug 1/5/10/15/20, or Jul 25/30 for the two cycles that hadn't recurred yet) — none left overdue/stuck-pending; the app's own confirm-on-arrival flow takes over cleanly from here.
  - **Reimbursable pattern (Juan only):** 3 expense/income pairs across June–July (Grab+parking ₱1,200, WFH dock ₱3,500, client-visit lunch ₱2,800), each followed 1–3 weeks later by a matching Reimbursement income — both categories flagged `exclude_from_analysis`.

Maria: Cash ₱120 · GCash ₱815 · Bank ₱25,001 · Credit Card −₱1,400. Joint Bank ₱20,400. All positive except the two credit cards, which are meant to carry a debt.

## Item 2 — Google Sign-In (pulled from Post-V1 Horizon #1)

- **Status:** 📋 **PLANNED — GRILLED 2026-07-23, design locked ([ADR-0050](../adr/0050-google-sign-in-native-credential-manager.md)). Not yet built.** Model for the build: **Opus** (novel auth pathway, cross-ADR interactions — 0013/0021/0024). This grill session itself: Opus, medium effort. No schema/Room change; DataStore-free; adds one `buildConfigField` + auth deps only.
- **Request:** Alvin — book Google Sign-In as a concrete v1.7.0 item (Facebook Login, previously paired with it on the Horizon list, is being shelved instead — see [Item 3](#item-3--facebook-login-shelved-indefinitely)).
- **Origin:** [Post-V1 Horizon #1](project-build-progress.md) — "Google Sign-In — Supabase OAuth + Android Credential Manager." One of the two SSO items explicitly out of V1 scope per `CLAUDE.md` ("Explicitly Out of Scope for V1 — Google / Facebook SSO"); pulled forward as an intentional post-V1 add.
- **Grill outcome — the load-bearing finding:** auth is **entirely SDK-session-driven**. `AuthRepositoryImpl.status` maps `client.auth.sessionStatus` → `AuthStatus`, and MainActivity's `Authenticated` branch (`accountSwitchGuard.onAuthenticated` → `ensureCurrentUserRow()` → schedule + await `syncEngine.sync()` → `shouldShowOnboarding()`) fires off **session status alone**, never the sign-up path. So Google Sign-In's whole job is *make a Supabase session exist*; the ADR-0013 users-row bootstrap, the ADR-0024 onboarding gate, and the ADR-0021 account-switch purge all run unchanged and method-agnostic. This collapsed most of the booking's "open questions" into non-issues. Full rationale + rejected alternatives in **[ADR-0050](../adr/0050-google-sign-in-native-credential-manager.md)**.
- **Decisions (each a grilled fork):**
  1. **Native Credential Manager, not OAuth redirect** — on-device Google ID token → `client.auth.signInWith(IDToken)`. The Custom-Tab redirect flow (which would reuse the existing `login-callback` deep link) was rejected for login on UX grounds. This is the current Google/Supabase-recommended path (the legacy `GoogleSignInClient` SDK is deprecated).
  2. **Hand-rolled thin client, not `compose-auth`** — a small Android-layer `GoogleCredentialClient` (`androidx.credentials` + `googleid`, raw + SHA-256-hashed nonce; takes an **Activity** context, never stores it) → `AuthRepository.signInWithGoogleIdToken(idToken, nonce)` → `SignInWithGoogleUseCase` → `AuthViewModel.signInWithGoogle(activity)`. Keeps Google on the same ViewModel→UseCase→Repository spine as email/password (uniform `AuthError`/spinner/lockout). `compose-auth` rejected — puts the auth call in the Composable, breaking layering.
  3. **Display name from Google claims via read-time fallback** — onboarding has no name-entry step, so a Google user's name must come from Google's `full_name`/`name` claims (Google doesn't set `display_name`, the key we read). Fix: `CurrentUserProvider.displayName()` resolves `display_name ?: full_name ?: name`. Email users unaffected. Write-time normalize rejected (extra network call).
  4. **Automatic account linking, relied upon** — Supabase auto-links a Google login to an existing account when both emails are verified; the app already requires verification before first login, so email+password accounts are always verified and the match lands as the *same user id* (data + couple pairing intact, no purge). Enforced by the Supabase dashboard default; no app code. The unverified-account takeover risk can't occur here.
  5. **UI: both modes, one "Continue with Google" button** — outlined, official Google "G" mark, below the primary button after an "or" divider, shown in **both** sign-in and sign-up (the tap creates/signs-in/links identically). Needs the Google "G" logo drawable added to `res/`.
  6. **Error handling — three-way:** dismissed sheet (`GetCredentialCancellationException`) → **silent**; no Google account on device (`NoCredentialException`) → specific message; anything else → one generic "couldn't sign in" (reuse `NETWORK` copy on connectivity). New `AuthError.GOOGLE_NO_ACCOUNT` + `GOOGLE_SIGN_IN_FAILED`; independent `isGoogleSubmitting` flag so the Google button spins without touching the email button.
  7. **No auto-select** on `GetGoogleIdOption` (picker always shows; explicit action) — so no `clearCredentialState()` plumbing on sign-out; existing sign-out is already method-agnostic.
  8. **Config per-flavor, staging-only** — Google **Web** OAuth client ID (server client ID — *not* the Android client ID, the classic failure trap) via gitignored `local.properties` → `buildConfigField`, matching the Supabase keys. Prod Supabase doesn't exist yet.
- **Email verification** → non-issue: a Google identity is pre-verified, so `signInWith(IDToken)` yields a session directly; no `EMAIL_NOT_CONFIRMED` path.
- **External prerequisites (build is dead until done — checklist):** (1) Google Cloud project + OAuth consent screen; (2) a **Web** OAuth client → its ID into `local.properties` + the Supabase dashboard; (3) Android OAuth client(s) with **three** SHA-1s registered — local **debug** keystore, **upload** key, and **Play App Signing** key (Play Console → Setup → App signing), because testers get the Play-re-signed build; (4) Supabase dashboard → Auth → Providers → **enable Google**, paste the Web client ID, confirm the same-email-linking default is on.
- **In-app linking is NOT in this item** — connecting Google to an already-signed-in account needs `linkIdentity(Google)` (OAuth **redirect** flow; supabase-kt has no native-ID-token link), so it's split to **[Item 13](#item-13--in-app-connect-google-account-linkidentity)**. Until it ships, an email user links implicitly: sign out → Continue with Google with the matching Gmail → auto-link (matching email only).
- **Tier-1 tests (JVM):** the Q3 display-name fallback resolution and the Q6 Credential-Manager-exception → `AuthError` mapping. The rest is Android-heavy → verify-by-running (real device — Credential Manager needs one; Alvin's on-device self-test loop).
- **Verify (at build):** on-device — first-time Google sign-in on a fresh account routes through onboarding then lands in the app with the Google name showing (not initials); a returning Google user signs straight in; an email user who signs out and taps Continue with Google with a matching Gmail lands in their *existing* account (data intact); dismissing the sheet shows no error; no-Google-account device shows the specific message. `testStagingDebugUnitTest` + `assembleStagingDebug` green.

## Item 5 — Settings → Finance: currency code labels black-on-black in dark mode

- **Status:** ✅ **DONE `4088449`** — on-device verified by Alvin (Settings → Finance and onboarding's Currency step, both surfaces). **Model: Sonnet, low effort** — a one-line color fix matching an already-diagnosed, already-fixed bug pattern (the Item 8 Slice 6a `MonthStepperRow` / Slice 6h `AccentColorPicker` "black-fallback under transparent Scaffold" bug); no grill needed. No schema/Room change.
- **Request:** Alvin — "settings>finance in dark mode currency names like PHP USD are black font color." Confirmed 2026-07-23 the same bug also shows in the onboarding Currency step.
- **Root cause:** [CurrencySymbolPicker.kt](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/core/ui/CurrencySymbolPicker.kt)'s `CurrencySwatch` rendered the currency code caption (`Text(symbol.code, ...)`, e.g. "PHP"/"USD") under the glyph circle with **no explicit color**. Both `FinanceScreen.kt` (Settings → Finance) and `OnboardingCurrencyScreen.kt` host the shared `CurrencyGrid` inside a `Scaffold(containerColor = Color.Transparent)`; `contentColorFor(Color.Transparent)` resolves to `Color.Unspecified`, and Compose's `Text` falls back to its hardcoded black default — same mechanism as the two prior fixes, just never caught on this shared component. Confirmed both surfaces share the exact same `CurrencyGrid` call (no separate onboarding copy), so one fix covers both.
- **Change:** [CurrencySymbolPicker.kt](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/core/ui/CurrencySymbolPicker.kt) — gave the code-label `Text` an explicit `color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurface`, matching the file's existing convention. Did not touch the glyph-circle swatch itself, `CurrencyGrid`'s layout, or any other consumer.
- **Verify:** `assembleStagingDebug` + `testStagingDebugUnitTest` green (pure color-value change, no logic, no new tests needed). On-device verified by Alvin: Settings → Finance and onboarding's Currency step in dark mode both show legible (non-black) "PHP"/"USD"/etc. labels under each currency swatch; light mode unaffected.

## Item 6 — General export facility (CSV / PDF / ZIP, receipt photos included)

- **Status:** ✅ **Slice 1 (CSV) DONE `798e215`** + ✅ **Slice 2 (PDF/ZIP, receipt photos) DONE `bd36116`** (both 2026-07-24, on-device verified). Slice 1: Sonnet, medium effort. Slice 2: **Opus, medium effort** (Supabase Storage egress path, `PdfDocument`/`ZipOutputStream` layout, the `EXPORT_WITH_ATTACHMENTS` entitlement gate, and a cross-feature `transaction_images` repository change — not a pure pattern-follow). Grilled 2026-07-23 (Opus, medium effort), built + on-device verified 2026-07-24 against the original inherits-Records'-filter design — then Slice 1 was **re-grilled 2026-07-24 (Sonnet, medium effort)** after Alvin flagged a discoverability gap in that design (see "Re-grill" below) and rebuilt to match, catching and fixing one bug along the way (the "What to include" label was falling back to "All transactions" whenever the date range went invalid, even with a filter applied — fixed by observing accounts/categories independently of range validity). **No ADR** — every decision is local to one feature; export reads existing repositories and writes a file, changing no invariant a future slice could violate (contrast ADR-0049, which changed what Analysis/Budgets/Combined *count*, or ADR-0050/0051's novel auth pathways).
- **Request (reframed during the original grill):** the booking was "export my reimbursable transactions to submit to my employer" (the ADR-0049 `exclude_from_analysis` pair, [Item 43](v1.6.9.md#item-43)). Alvin **rejected the reimbursable-specific framing on the first question**: *"I don't want us to get involved with that, I want our facility to export be general for general use… multiple options of exporting: CSV for without attachments, PDF with attachments, ZIP with attachments where it's easy to identify which is which."* Reimbursables are the **motivating use case, not the scope**.
- **Scope-list consequence:** this **un-shelves** [deferred.md](deferred.md#csv--pdf-export)'s "CSV / PDF export" (ex-Post-V1-Horizon #7, shelved 2026-07-07) and requires striking **"CSV / PDF export"** from `CLAUDE.md`'s *Explicitly Out of Scope for V1* list. Both edits made with this write-up.
- **Grill outcome — the load-bearing findings (original grill, still true):**
  1. **Receipt photos are not on the phone.** [TransactionImageUploader.kt:57](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/data/upload/TransactionImageUploader.kt#L57) calls `file.delete()` the moment a receipt uploads; the row keeps only an *authenticated* Supabase Storage URL (private `receipts` bucket). Coil's disk cache is an eviction cache, not addressable storage. **So any export carrying photos must hit the network** — the one place this offline-first app cannot be offline.
  2. **PDF needs no library.** `android.graphics.pdf.PdfDocument` is in the framework (API 19+, minSdk 26). The booking's assumed "needs a renderer library" cost does not exist — **zero new dependencies for the whole item**.
  3. **A free user has zero receipt photos** ([subscription-paywall-design.md:220](subscription-paywall-design.md) — free cap revised 1→0 in v1.6.7 Item 9), which makes the attachment formats premium-by-implication and decides the gating line on its own (decision 3).
- **Re-grill 2026-07-24 — why the original "inherit Records' filter" design changed:** Slice 1 built + on-device-verified fine against the original design (Export silently scoped to whatever filter/month Records happened to be showing). Walking through the built flow, Alvin identified a real UX gap: **a user who wants to export *only* a subset (e.g. just their reimbursables) has no way to discover that — the Export sheet only ever showed 3 date-range buttons, with no visible path to "filter first."** The fix isn't a smaller tweak; it inverts decision 1 below. Full transcript-level rationale in conversation; the resulting decisions:
  1. **Export owns its own filter step, fully decoupled from Records (supersedes original decision 1).** Tapping Export always opens **blank** — no inherited filter, no inherited viewed-month — so scoping is always a deliberate, visible, in-flow choice rather than silently-carried browsing state. Records' own filter (Item 7) is unaffected and untouched by this — the two are now fully independent.
  2. **One sheet, filter visible-but-optional (not a mandatory wizard step).** Rejected a sequential "filter screen → Apply → date-range screen → Export" wizard: it forces every "just export this month" user through a filter screen they don't need. Instead the export sheet gets a single **"What to include" row** (reads *"All transactions ›"* by default) sitting above the date range — tapping it opens the filter, leaving it alone exports everything. Solves the discoverability gap (the row itself teaches the capability) without taxing the common case.
  3. **The filter sheet is the same shared component Records uses, not a copy (extracted from `TransactionsScreen.kt`).** Preserves the original "no second filter UI drifting out of sync" principle even though the sheet is now shown in two places — Records and Export both call one `TransactionFilterSheet`, same four dimensions, same chip/inverted-amount behavior. Presented **stacked** (a second `ModalBottomSheet` on top of the export sheet) — Export is a lightweight, occasional action, not worth promoting to a full screen. Apply commits + recomputes the count; Clear → "All transactions"; dismiss discards without changing the export's scope.
  4. **"What to include" row label:** *"All transactions ›"* unfiltered; the **category name** (e.g. *"Reimbursable ›"*) when exactly one category is the only constraint; **"Filtered ›"** for anything more complex (2+ categories, or any type/account/amount constraint). Ties to nothing else now (the old filename scope-word is gone, decision 7 below) — this is purely the row's own label logic.
  5. **Date range: two editable From/To fields, not preset buttons (supersedes the original 3-chip picker).** Default **1st-of-current-month → today** (month-to-date), always the *current* month regardless of which month Records happens to be paged to — Export no longer reads Records' viewed month at all. Each field is a tappable single-date field opening a plain date picker. From-after-To disables Export with an inline note (mirrors Item 7's inverted-range guard). Rejected the M3 `DateRangePicker` big-calendar widget — heavier than the task, and forces re-picking both ends to nudge one.
  6. **Filename: bare `LoveIpon-{from}_{to}.csv`, day-precise, no scope word (supersedes the original decision 7).** Alvin's call: drop the category-name-in-filename idea entirely (`LoveIpon-Reimbursable-2026-07.csv` → gone) in favor of one constant, predictable shape — `LoveIpon-2026-07-01_2026-07-24.csv`, collapsing to a single date if From == To. Day-precise because the new default (month-to-date) is essentially never a whole calendar month, so a month-only filename (`2026-07`) would almost always be wrong/misleading anyway.
  7. **Live transaction count stays, demoted.** Kept as plain feedback (not the old "safety disclosure" — that rationale is gone now that scope is always visibly chosen) — recomputes as the filter/range change, and doubles as the empty-state signal (decision 8).
  8. **Zero-match range disables Export (Q8).** Count line reads *"No transactions to export"* and the Export button is disabled — rejected shipping a header-only CSV as confusing/useless; catches "you narrowed it too far" before an empty file goes out.
- **Decisions carried over unchanged from the original grill (apply to both slices):**
  1. **Entry point = overflow menu, holding Recurring *and* Export.** Records' title row is **filter + eye + ⋮**; Recurring moved into the ⋮ menu alongside Export…, keeping the surface to 3 direct glyphs instead of 4. ⚠️ Moves shipped UI — Recurring becomes a two-tap navigation. Deliberate, Alvin's call, on-device verified 2026-07-24 (Recurring still navigates correctly from the menu).
  2. **CSV free; PDF + ZIP Premium.** New soft gate `EXPORT_WITH_ATTACHMENTS` (tap PDF/ZIP on free → paywall) in ADR-0044's feature map; **no gate on CSV, ever** — data portability stays free, CSV costs nothing (no Storage egress), and free users have zero photos anyway (non-cannibalizing by construction). Ships **dormant** (kill-switch OFF) per the standing build stance.
  3. **Photos: use-local-if-present, else download.** Three guardrails: **(a)** offline blocks PDF/ZIP but never CSV, shown upfront; **(b)** a missing photo prints "Receipt unavailable" rather than silently skipping; **(c)** photos stream one at a time, never held in memory together.
  4. **PDF/ZIP cap = 100 photos** (~25MB, ≈1 min on mediocre PH mobile), refused before the tap with a narrowing message. No cap on CSV (text-only, sub-second even at thousands of rows).
  5. **Progress is numeric, cancellable, foreground-only** — *"Downloading receipts… 34 of 112"*. Cancel deletes the partial file; leaving the screen cancels.
  6. **Share sheet only; temporary file** in `cacheDir/exports/` via `FileProvider`. Transmission, not a stored document — swept on every app start (verified 2026-07-24: 2 leftover files cleared after a force-stop + relaunch). Rejected save-to-Downloads (the share sheet's own "Save to Files" already covers it).
  7. **Contents: own rows, private rows included, real amounts.** `isPrivate` rows included (private = hidden from partner, not from self); the privacy eye never masks the file; own rows only (no Combined/couple export in this item).
  8. **CSV shape.** Columns `Date · Type · Category · Account · Note · Amount · Receipts`, one row per transaction, **Total row at the bottom**. Amounts are bare signed numbers (`480.00` / `-500.00` — income positive, expense/transfer negative, no `₱`, no thousands separators) so the Total equals the exact column sum and Excel/Sheets parse them as numbers. Transfers render the destination in Category as `→ BPI Savings`; settlements render `Debt settlement`. **Alvin's call, confirmed 2026-07-24:** signed amounts stay even though an all-expense reimbursable export nets a negative Total — matches a bank-statement convention over a "claim total" convention.
  9. **PDF/ZIP row↔photo linkage (Slice 2, unaffected by the re-grill):** page 1 is the claim sheet (numbered receipt-bearing rows `#3`), pages 2+ carry one receipt per page at near-full size with a caption; ZIP carries `transactions.csv` + `receipts/03_....jpg`. No signature/approval line (general service, not one employer's form). Description falls back note → category name → type.
- **Change — two slices:**
  - **Slice 1 — CSV (free, no network). `DONE 798e215`, 2026-07-24.** Built to the original design, on-device verified, then re-built same day to the re-grilled design above and re-verified on-device. Records overflow menu (Recurring + Export…) · export `ModalBottomSheet` with a live count, a **"What to include" row** opening a **shared, extracted** `TransactionFilterSheet` (stacked), and **From/To date fields** (MTD default) · `FileProvider` + paths XML + `ACTION_SEND` · CSV writer · bare day-precise filename builder · `cacheDir/exports` startup sweep. **No photos, no network, no gating.**
  - **Slice 2 — PDF + ZIP (premium, network). `DONE bd36116`, 2026-07-24.** Photo fetcher (`ReceiptFetcher`, local-else-download) · numeric progress + cancel (`ExportProgress`, partial file deleted on cancel/failure) · 100-photo pre-check (`AttachmentLimits`) · offline block (only when the scope has a photo needing download) · "Receipt unavailable" placeholder (PDF page + ZIP `_UNAVAILABLE.txt`, never silently skipped) · `PdfDocument` claim sheet + one-receipt-per-page layout (`PdfExporter`) · `ZipOutputStream` + extraction-safe naming (`ZipExporter`/`ZipEntryNaming`) · `EXPORT_WITH_ATTACHMENTS` `Feature` key wired **dormant** via `PremiumGate.observeLocked(INDIVIDUAL)`. Row↔photo numbering + description fallback extracted as pure `ReceiptNumbering`/`ExportDescription`. `ExportRow` now carries `List<ExportPhoto>` (id/localPath/url) instead of a bare count; new `ObserveTransactionImagesUseCase` + `TransactionImageDao.observeAllActive()` (includes pre-upload rows, unlike the combined-view URL-only observe); `StorageUrlRewrite.toObjectRef()` recovers (bucket, path) from a stored URL for the SDK download. Inherits Slice 1's filter/range sheet unchanged. **No new Gradle dependency** (`android.graphics.pdf.PdfDocument` + `java.util.zip` are stock); no schema/Room change.
    - **Two bugs found + fixed during on-device verification** (not by review): (1) every receipt page's footer read "page 2" — the page counter only advanced inside the claim sheet, so all receipt pages inherited `claimSheetPages + 1`; fixed to number continuously across the whole document (resilient to a multi-page claim sheet). (2) captions printed `₱-2,450.00`; the sign belongs outside the glyph → `-₱2,450.00` (receipt captions only — table amounts stay bare so the column aligns).
  - **Does not change:** any schema, Room table, DAO, repository, or sync path (export is read-only over existing repositories, per `CLAUDE.md`'s scalability principle — *"a future export UseCase must be able to reuse them"*); the uploader's delete-after-upload behavior; the Combined view; the privacy eye's display semantics; Item 7's own Records filter (now fully independent of Export's). **No new Gradle dependency.**
  - **Doc edits landing with the build:** un-shelve [deferred.md](deferred.md#csv--pdf-export) → point at this item; strike CSV/PDF export from `CLAUDE.md`'s out-of-scope list; add `EXPORT_WITH_ATTACHMENTS` to [subscription-paywall-design.md](subscription-paywall-design.md) §8 map + §9 feature-key table; `CONTEXT.md` gains **Export scope** + **Attachment bundle** (added with this write-up).
- **Tier-1 tests (JVM) — pure functions only:** (1) CSV row serialization per type (income/expense/transfer-with-`→ destination`/settlement); (2) amount formatting is bare-numeric, signed, locale-independent; (3) note/category/type description fallback chain; (4) total row equals the sum of rows; (5) filename builder — bare `LoveIpon-{from}_{to}` shape, day-precise, single-date collapse when From == To, filesystem-unsafe characters n/a now (no scope word); (6) month-to-date range resolution (1st of month → today, any day-of-month); (7) "What to include" row label logic (all/single-category/filtered); (8) empty-result → disabled predicate. PDF drawing, the share sheet, and the downloader are Android/network-heavy → **verify by running**. **Slice 2 added (26 new cases):** `ReceiptNumbering` (8 — only receipt-bearing rows numbered, `#3a/#3b/#3c` multi-photo suffixes, ordinals across the whole export, download-count), `ZipEntryNaming` (8 — zero-padded claim number, date + slugged description, filesystem-safe, `_UNAVAILABLE.txt` same-stem), `ExportDescription` (6 — note→category→type fallback), `AttachmentLimits` (4 — 100 allowed / 101 refused boundary), plus 5 `StorageUrlRewrite.toObjectRef` cases.

## Item 7 — Records page filter feature

- **Status:** ✅ **DONE `4013eef`** (2026-07-24, Sonnet, medium effort, on-device verified by Alvin). Grilled 2026-07-23 (Opus, medium effort), design locked. **No schema/Room/DAO change** — filtering is client-side over rows already in memory. **No ADR:** every decision is local to one screen's presentation layer; there's no cross-cutting rule a future slice could violate (contrast Items 2/13, which earned ADR-0050/0051 for novel auth pathways).
- **Request:** Alvin — add filtering to the Records (Transactions) tab, scoped to the currently-visible month: filter by category, filter by account, and filter by amount-spent range (min/max). **No date filter** — the page already separates transactions by date/day-header, so a date-range filter would be redundant. **Filter only, no sorting.**
- **Grill outcome — the load-bearing findings:**
  1. **The `combine` ceiling is a non-issue if the filter goes *upstream*.** `TransactionsViewModel`'s main `combine` is genuinely maxed at 5 flows with **three trailing `.combine`s** already stacked (`isRefreshing`, `deepHistoryLocked`, `observePrivacyMode`), and filtering must happen *before* `DayGrouping.groupByDay` — which is built *inside* that combine, so a trailing combine can't do it. Resolved by filtering one level up instead of adding a 6th flow (see Change below).
  2. **Every filterable field is already on `Transaction`** (`categoryId`, `accountId`, `toAccountId`, `amount`, `type`, `isSettlement`) — no join against the account/category *name* maps is needed to filter, so the filter is a pure list→list function over raw domain models.
  3. **Records is already month-windowed** (`transactionsInRange = viewedMonth.flatMapLatest { observeTransactions(start, end) }`), so the candidate set is tens of rows, already in memory — which decides the query question below on its own.
- **Decisions (each a grilled fork):**
  1. **Filter icon → bottom sheet, not an inline chip row (Q1).** Three-plus dimensions, two of them multi-select over unbounded lists, plus a min/max numeric input — none of that fits a horizontal `PlayfulChip` strip like Categories' All/Income/Expense `FilterRow`. A filter icon joins the `PlayfulScreenTitle` actions (beside Recurring + the privacy eye) and opens a `ModalBottomSheet`. The icon carries an **accent dot whenever a filter is applied**, so the user always knows why rows are hidden.
  2. **Client-side, filtered upstream of the main combine (Q2).** Rejected a new `TransactionDao` variant: SQL `IN (...)` lists would churn on every chip toggle to filter a set that's already resident. Instead a `filter: MutableStateFlow<TransactionFilter>` feeds `filteredInRange = combine(transactionsInRange, filter) { txns, f -> f.apply(txns) }`, and `filteredInRange` **replaces `transactionsInRange` in the main combine's first slot** — tuple stays at 5, grouping runs over already-filtered rows, and `TransactionFilter.apply()` falls out as a pure, unit-testable function. Picker options come from the `accounts`/`categories` flows already in the combine; no new source.
  3. **AND across dimensions, OR within one; empty selection = unconstrained (Q3).** `(category ∈ sel) AND (account ∈ sel) AND (type ∈ sel) AND (min ≤ amount ≤ max)`.
  4. **The no-category row types, handled deliberately (Q3).** **Transfers** (`categoryId = null`) and **settlements** (`categoryId = null, isSettlement = true`) can never match a **category** filter — correct, they have none. But an **account** filter matches a transfer on **either `accountId` or `toAccountId`** (filtering to "Credit Card" must surface a Bank→Card paydown), and matches a settlement on its `accountId`. This asymmetry — category narrows to categorized rows, account spans everything touching that account — is intentional, not a bug.
  5. **Amount range = absolute, inclusive, independently optional (Q3/Q9).** Applied to the stored-positive `amount` on **all** row types (sign is derived at display). Parsed to `BigDecimal?` per the money convention — blank or unparseable → `null` = unbounded on that side, never zero, never a crash. Both bounds inclusive. **Inverted range (min > max)** → inline "Minimum can't be larger than maximum" error + **Apply disabled**; auto-swapping was rejected as silently changing what the user typed. **No privacy-mode coupling** — the eye masks *displayed* amounts; a range the user types themselves leaks nothing, so the fields stay live when privacy is on (stated explicitly so it doesn't get "fixed" later).
  6. **Session-scoped state; survives month-stepping; NOT persisted (Q4).** The filter is independent of `viewedMonth` (free, given decision 2) so you can hold a "Groceries on the Credit Card" lens while paging Jun→Jul→Aug — resetting per month-step would make it near-useless. It lives as a plain ViewModel `MutableStateFlow` and dies with the ViewModel/process. **DataStore rejected:** privacy mode and palette are global *identity* prefs; a transaction filter is a transient *exploration lens*, and persisting it invites the "why is Records empty after reboot?" confusion. The active dot (decision 1) plus the empty-state Clear (decision 8) are the in-session mitigation.
  7. **Explicit Apply, not live-apply (Q8).** The sheet owns a **draft** `TransactionFilter` seeded from the applied one; **Apply** commits it to the ViewModel flow, **dismissing discards** the draft, **Clear** resets to none. The active dot reflects only *applied* state. Live-apply was rejected: it reflows the list on every digit of the amount fields (a half-typed "5" filters to ≥₱5 for a frame) and leaves no way to cancel a change.
  8. **A distinct fourth empty state (Q5).** Reusing "No transactions this month" when rows exist but are filtered out reads as data loss. New branch — title *"No matches"*, body *"No transactions this month match your filters."*, plus an inline **"Clear filters"** action so the user can escape without reopening the sheet. Keyed on `dayGroups.isEmpty() && filterIsActive && hadRowsBeforeFilter`, so the three existing empty states (`!canAdd`, never-any-transaction, empty-month) all still win in their own cases.
  9. **Filter picker is active-only (Q6).** Mirrors the Add/Edit pickers and the v1.6.7 Item 5 picker-vs-display split: display maps stay `includeArchived = true` so a historical row keeps its real "Groceries" label, but an archived entity is **not** a filter criterion. Accepted cost: rows under a just-archived category are visible-but-not-isolatable — a genuine edge (archiving is rare, filtering by a freshly-archived category rarer), and flipping the picker source is a one-line change if a tester asks.
  10. **Ledger-list-only scope; icon gated on `hasAnyTransactionEver` (Q7).** The pinned `PendingConfirmationsCard` ("To confirm") and `ComingUpCard` ("Coming up") are **relative to today, not the viewed month**, and are a different concern (recurring arrivals, not ledger history) — the filter **does not touch them**. The icon is gated on `hasAnyTransactionEver` (not `canAdd`, which gates the stepper/FAB): nothing to filter on a fresh install, but the icon stays available in an empty *month* so the user can check whether a filter is what emptied it.
  11. **A transaction-*type* filter added to scope (Q11, Alvin's call).** Not in the original booking; surfaced during the grill and accepted. `type` is already on `Transaction` and is a 3-value enum, so it's one more `PlayfulChip` row with no picker source and zero architectural change — and it closes the "isolate my transfers" gap that the category axis structurally cannot (decision 4). **Final dimension count: four** — Categories, Accounts, Types, Amount range.
  12. **Multi-select mechanics (Q10).** Categories/Accounts/Types each render as a wrapping `FlowRow` of toggling `PlayfulChip`s. **No explicit "All" chip** — empty selection *is* all, per decision 3; an "All" chip creates an ambiguous third state. Section header shows a subtle "All" hint when nothing is selected. **One footer-level Clear**, no per-section clears (deselecting is already direct; keeps the sheet from going button-heavy). Long lists just scroll natively in the `ModalBottomSheet`.
- **Change:**
  - **New** `TransactionFilter` domain-ish model + pure `apply(List<Transaction>): List<Transaction>` (four dimensions, semantics per decisions 3–5), plus the inverted-range validity predicate that drives Apply's enabled state.
  - [TransactionsViewModel.kt](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/presentation/TransactionsViewModel.kt) — add the `filter` `MutableStateFlow` + `filteredInRange` upstream combine (decision 2); swap it into the main combine's first slot; add `applyFilter(...)`/`clearFilter()`.
  - [TransactionsUiState.kt](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/presentation/TransactionsUiState.kt) — carry the applied filter (for the active dot + sheet seeding), `filterIsActive`, and `hadRowsBeforeFilter` (for decision 8's empty-state branch).
  - [TransactionsScreen.kt](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/presentation/TransactionsScreen.kt) — filter `IconButton` + active dot in the `PlayfulScreenTitle` actions; new `TransactionFilterSheet` composable (draft state, four sections, Apply/Clear); new "No matches" empty-state branch.
  - **Does not change:** `TransactionDao`/`TransactionRepository`/`ObserveTransactionsUseCase` (no new query), any schema/Room table, the recurring/forecast cards, the month stepper, the DEEP_HISTORY back-wall, or the privacy eye. Sorting stays out of scope per Alvin's framing.
- **Tier-1 tests (JVM) — all against the pure `TransactionFilter.apply()`:** (1) `NONE` → input unchanged; (2) category match/exclude; (3) account match on `accountId`; (4) type match; (5) amount min-only / max-only / both, **inclusive at both boundaries**; (6) **transfer matches on `toAccountId`**; (7) **category filter hides transfers and settlements**; (8) settlement matches an account filter on `accountId`; (9) OR within a dimension (two categories → rows from both); (10) AND across dimensions (category X + account Y → intersection, not union); (11) blank/unparseable amount → `null` bound, unconstrained; (12) inverted range → flagged invalid. The empty-state selection logic is `TransactionsUiState` wiring → verify-by-running, per "test ViewModels once stable."
- **Built as planned, with one polish fix found during on-device verification:** the Category/Account `FlowRow`s only had `horizontalArrangement` spacing, so wrapped chip rows sat flush against each other (cramped). Added `verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp)` to all three sheet `FlowRow`s. The sheet's `verticalScroll` wrapper is unaffected (was already in place for overflow on smaller screens / longer lists).
- **Verify:** `testStagingDebugUnitTest` (15/15 new `TransactionFilterTest` cases) + `assembleStagingDebug` green. On-device verified on a Medium_Phone AVD against real staging data (testdev7): filter icon appears only once a transaction exists; sheet opens with four sections, each showing an "All" hint; toggling chips changes nothing until **Apply**; dismissing (scrim/back) discards the draft; the active dot appears/clears correctly; a zero-match combination shows "No matches" with a working inline Clear (and the "Coming up" card stayed unfiltered); a genuinely empty month (no rows at all) correctly falls to the plain "No transactions this month" state, not "No matches"; the filter **survives month-stepping** (July → June) but is gone after a force-stop relaunch (session-scoped, confirmed).

## Item 8 — Prompt to create a counterpart category when saving a reimbursable category

- **Status:** ✅ **DONE `89f57cd`** (2026-07-23, Sonnet, medium effort as booked) — reused the existing `PendingCategoryDelete` confirm-dialog shape already in the same ViewModel (state holds a pending confirmation, `PlayfulDialog` renders it, VM sets/clears it). No schema/Room change — reuses the ADR-0049 `excludeFromAnalysis` flag and the existing `UpsertCategoryUseCase`, no new entity/column.
- **Request:** Alvin — today [Item 43](v1.6.9.md#item-43) (ADR-0049) lets a user flip "Exclude from spending reports" on a category, but nothing nudges them to create the matching counterpart (expense↔income) that makes the pass-through pattern actually work (per the discussion above: without both legs, the balance looks permanently off). When the user taps Save on a category editor with the flag ON, intercept the save and ask whether they want to create the counterpart now, before persisting:
  - Expense reimbursable created → *"Do you want to create an income reimbursement category for this? This is where you'll log when you get paid back."* (Yes/No)
  - Income reimbursable created → *"Do you want to create an expense reimbursement category for this? This is where you'll log when you spend your reimbursement."* (Yes/No) — covers the advance-then-spend direction (e.g. employer gives a phone allowance upfront; the expense leg is logged when the employee actually buys the phone).
- **Confirmed in conversation:**
  - If **Yes** → do **not** auto-name/auto-derive the counterpart. Show a second prompt asking the user to type the counterpart category's name (simple text-input dialog), then create it (opposite `CategoryType`, `excludeFromAnalysis = true`) alongside the original, both via `UpsertCategoryUseCase`. Icon/color default to the same values as the original category (only the name is user-prompted; not worth a second icon/color picker for a same-flow side effect).
  - If **No** (or dialog dismissed) → save just the original category, exactly like today. No forced choice — dismissal behaves like No.
  - This prompt fires on **create** only where the flag is being turned on; **does not** apply retroactively to existing categories that already have the flag (no migration/backfill prompt).
- **Change:**
  - [CategoriesUiState.kt](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/categories/presentation/CategoriesUiState.kt) — new pending-confirmation state alongside `PendingCategoryDelete` (e.g. `pendingCounterpartPrompt: Category?` for the Yes/No step, `pendingCounterpartNameInput: Category?` for the name-input step) — two sequential dialogs, not one.
  - [CategoriesViewModel.kt](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/categories/presentation/CategoriesViewModel.kt) — `save()` (currently lines 144-168): when `state.excludeFromAnalysis` is true and this is a create (or the flag is newly turned on), branch into the confirm-dialog state instead of calling `UpsertCategoryUseCase` immediately; add handlers for Yes/No and for the name-input submit that create both categories via two `UpsertCategoryUseCase` calls. No new UseCase needed.
  - [CategoriesScreen.kt](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/categories/presentation/CategoriesScreen.kt) — two new `PlayfulDialog` renders (Yes/No prompt, then name-input prompt), copy-worded per direction as above, mirroring how the delete-confirm dialog is rendered near lines 207-233.
  - **Does not change:** `Category` domain model, `UpsertCategoryUseCase`, `CategoryRepository`/`CategoryRepositoryImpl` (the `excludeFromAnalysis` passthrough there is already correct, per earlier on-device fix), the onboarding-seeded "Reimbursable"/"Reimbursement" pair, or any Analysis/Budgets/Combined exclusion logic.
- **Built as planned, with one deliberate deviation:** the original category is saved **immediately** on Save (unchanged from today), not deferred until the Yes/No answer as the "Change" bullet above sketched — if the app is killed between Save and answering the prompt, the category the user actually asked for survives; only the optional counterpart is lost. Verified empirically (see below).
- **Follow-up refinement (mid-build, Alvin's request):** step 2's bare "Name" field had no context, unlike step 1's full sentence. Added the same direction-specific helper sentence above the field (extracted into a shared `counterpartHelperText()` so both dialogs can't drift out of sync) plus an "e.g. Reimbursement" placeholder in the field itself.
- **Verify:** `testStagingDebugUnitTest` green — 161/161 including 7 new `CategoriesViewModelTest` cases (expense→income, income→expense, flag-off no-op, edit-never-fires, blank-name guard, full create flow with icon/color inheritance, dismiss-is-No). `assembleStagingDebug` green. On-device: expense→income and income→expense directions confirmed by Alvin; explicit No, scrim-tap dismiss, edit-does-not-fire, blank-name guard, and abandon-mid-flow (force-stop between "Yes" and naming, to test the deviation above) all verified on an emulator, cross-checked against the local Room DB (`excludeFromAnalysis`/`type`/icon/color columns all correct on every row, no orphan rows from the abandoned attempt).

- **Status:** 📋 **PLANNED — GRILLED 2026-07-23 (Opus, medium effort), design locked. Not yet built.** Model for the build: **Opus** (touches the ADR-0004/0005/0011 partner-data render boundary; not a pure pattern-follow). **No schema/Room change** — the derived banner renders over data already synced (both partners' `accent_color`, `avatar_motif`, `couple_name`); zero new field.
- **Request:** originally [Post-V1 Horizon #9](project-build-progress.md) ("Profile & couple photo upload"), pulled into [v1.6.7.md Item 3](v1.6.7.md#item-3--profile--couple-photo-upload-pulled-from-post-v1-horizon-9) and grilled 2026-07-22 (Opus session), which staged the resolved concept into 3 legs of differing weight. **Leg 1 (motif avatars) shipped** as v1.6.7 Item 3 (`f75cf4d`). Legs 2 + 3 were said to be "deferred to v1.6.8.md," but v1.6.8's charter was reset to a single-fix release (2026-07-22) before either leg got its own item number or grill — they fell through the cracks. Re-booked here.
- **Grill outcome — the unifying finding (Q1):** Items 9 and 10 are **not** the "derived vs. own" either/or the source grill framed them as — they're **one layered feature**: the derived banner is the **free default**, and Item 10's uploaded photo is the **premium override**, occupying the **same slot**. A free/lapsed couple always falls cleanly back to the derived layer (freeze-friendly, §2.1). So Item 9 builds the derived layer + the surface; [Item 10](#item-10--premium-couple-photo-upload-item-3-leg-3-pulled-from-post-v1-horizon-9) layers the photo onto it.
- **Surface (Q2):** the **Couple identity card** only — `PairedContent`'s Blush [PlayfulCard] in [CoupleOverviewBody.kt](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/couple/presentation/CoupleOverviewBody.kt) (L169, which already renders both `MotifAvatar`s + couple name + "Paired with X"). A ~120dp hero strip at the **top of that card**. Explicitly **not** the Combined view (`CombinedBody` is deliberately chrome-less — a hero there fights its purpose and re-touches Item 8 Slice 4 a third time).
- **Derived recipe (Q3):** a **two-tone horizontal gradient blending both partners' `accent_color`s** (`Brush.horizontalGradient(listOf(accentA, accentB))`), with the couple name + both `MotifAvatar`s overlaid. Reuses the exact accent-color identity system Leg 1 established — blue-partner + pink-partner reads instantly as *this specific couple*. Edge cases: **awaiting-partner** (only one accent known) → single-accent wash of the current user's color; **both accents identical** → valid near-solid (verify-by-running polish, not a design call). **Always-on, no toggle** — zero-config is the whole point of the free layer.
- **Change (Slice 1):**
  - **New component** `CoupleBanner` in [core/ui](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/core/ui/) (or `feature/couple/presentation/components`) — draws the hero strip; takes the two accents (+ partner-absent flag), couple name, and both motif keys.
  - Extract a pure `bannerBrushSpec(accentA, accentB?)` → gradient-stops-or-single-wash, so the derivation logic is unit-testable (the Compose render is verify-by-running).
  - Wire it into `PairedContent` above the existing name/label column.
  - **Does not change:** any schema, Room, sync, `couples`/`users` columns, or the Combined view.
- **Build order:** **Slice 1 of the two-slice arc** — ships first (immediate visible win, stable slot), on its own commit. [Item 10](#item-10--premium-couple-photo-upload-item-3-leg-3-pulled-from-post-v1-horizon-9) wraps it in Slice 2.
- **Tier-1 tests (JVM):** `bannerBrushSpec()` — two distinct accents → two-stop gradient; null partner accent → single wash; identical accents → valid near-solid.
- **Verify (at build):** on-device (paired staging couple) — the identity card shows the two-tone hero with both avatars + couple name; awaiting-partner state shows the single-accent wash; re-tints correctly across palette/dark-mode switches (avatars stay keyed to each user's stored `accent_color`, not a palette token). `testStagingDebugUnitTest` + `assembleStagingDebug` green.

## Item 10 — Premium couple-photo upload (Item 3 Leg 3, pulled from Post-V1 Horizon #9)

- **Status:** 📋 **PLANNED — GRILLED 2026-07-23 (Opus, medium effort), design locked. Not yet built.** Model for the build: **Opus** (spans Storage/RLS, a new dependency, the entitlement/`PlanLimits` gate per ADR-0044, and couple-shared state; not a pure pattern-follow). **Schema/Room change:** `couples.banner_url text` + a `set_couple_banner` RPC + a new `couple-banners` Storage bucket; **Room v28 → v29** (plain `@AutoMigration`, nullable). **Soft-blocked visibly:** entitlement enforcement is dormant app-wide (kill-switch OFF per CLAUDE.md's Monetization section) until the post-beta flip — the feature is buildable now but won't visibly lock/unlock until that flip.
- **Request:** same origin as [Item 9](#item-9--couple-banner-derived-layer-item-3-leg-2-pulled-from-post-v1-horizon-9) — Leg 3 of the [v1.6.7.md Item 3](v1.6.7.md#item-3--profile--couple-photo-upload-pulled-from-post-v1-horizon-9) grill, lost when v1.6.8.md's charter reset. Re-booked and grilled here as the **premium override** half of the unified couple-banner feature (see Item 9's Q1 finding).
- **Decisions (each a grilled fork):**
  1. **Per-couple, not per-user (Q4):** the photo is **one shared banner for the couple**, not a per-user avatar. Pointer on a new `couples.banner_url` column, written via a `set_couple_banner(p_url)` **SECURITY DEFINER RPC** (couples are RPC-write-only, ADR-0006/0008 — `CoupleTableSyncer`'s outbox is always empty; the changed row flows back on the next pull). The dormant `users.avatar_url` stays dormant (a separate per-user-photo feature is genuinely out of scope). This is the true "own" override of the derived *couple* banner — same slot as Item 9's gradient.
  2. **Storage (Q5):** new **private `couple-banners`** bucket, path `{couple_id}/{randomUUID}.jpg` (folder[1] = `couple_id` is the RLS key, mirroring `receipts`' folder[1] = `userId`). **Fresh filename each upload** → new `authenticatedUrl` → Coil never serves a stale banner (a fixed path + `upsert` would). `StorageAuthInterceptor`/`StorageUrlRewrite` is already **bucket-agnostic** — zero interceptor change.
  3. **RLS = one policy, no new function (Q5):** `bucket_id = 'couple-banners' and (storage.foldername(name))[1] = auth_couple_id()::text` for **both** SELECT and INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE. `auth_couple_id()` is already `SECURITY DEFINER` (verified live: owner `postgres`), so the ADR-0043 "wrap the visibility check in a definer function" trap is avoided for free — and both partners resolve the same couple, so **either can set the banner** (matches D1 either-partner governance).
  4. **Interactive crop (Q6/Q7):** **`com.mr0xf00:easycrop`** (pure-Compose cropper, Apache-2, Maven Central — fits CLAUDE.md's "no XML layouts ever" without AppCompat/View baggage), **aspect-locked to the banner ratio** (~3:1). Flow: `PickVisualMedia` → easycrop → post-crop **compress reusing the existing `CompressReceiptUseCase` recipe** (BitmapFactory → `createScaledBitmap` → JPEG 85%, ≤~1440px, file-size ceiling — real-cost discipline, storage is the load-bearing premium lever) → upload → RPC.
  5. **Gate (Q8):** **shared soft gate.** Scope = **shared** (D1 — either partner premium unlocks it for both). Type = **soft** ("Set couple photo" is visible + desirable; tapping while locked → paywall, like palettes). Lapse = **non-destructive revert-to-derived** (the G8 palette-reconciliation pattern): render photo **iff** `unlocked && banner_url != null`, else the derived gradient; the object + column are **retained** on lapse (§2.1 freeze) and **auto-restore** on re-grant — a pure read-time derivation, so flip-day and flip-back-OFF leave zero residue. Ships **dormant** (kill-switch OFF) → free couples *can* set a photo until the post-beta flip.
  6. **Storage cleanup — all three paths (Q9):** on **replace** (upload flow deletes the previous object), in **`delete_account`** (add a `couple-banners` delete under the caller's `{couple_id}/` prefix — the RPC already deletes storage objects as `postgres`), *and* in **`unpair`** (add the same one-line delete — verified live that `unpair` is already `postgres`-owned, so it holds the DELETE privilege with **no owner/grant change**; the delete is functionally independent of unpair's load-bearing bell/couple_id ordering, so it's ordering-safe; and unpair is the *more common* orphan path than account deletion, so skipping it would tidy the rare path and leak the common one). Note: an orphaned banner is already **unreadable by anyone** post-unpair (`auth_couple_id()` → null never matches the folder key) — cleanup is hygiene, not a leak fix.
- **Change (Slice 2):**
  - **Schema/sync:** `couples.banner_url text` in [schema.sql](../../supabase/schema.sql) + migration; thread `bannerUrl` through `CoupleDto`/`CoupleEntity`/`CoupleMapper` + the `Couple` domain model (exactly as `couple_name` is threaded); **Room v28 → v29** (`@AutoMigration`, nullable, null = derived). `set_couple_banner(p_url)` RPC (member-check + `update couples set banner_url = p_url` — bumps `server_rev` so it pulls back). New `couple-banners` bucket + the one RLS policy. Cleanup added to `delete_account` + `unpair`.
  - **Upload:** a `CoupleBannerUploader` (mirrors `TransactionImageUploader` — `authenticatedUrl(path)`, `couple-banners` bucket) + a UseCase orchestrating pick→crop→compress→upload→`set_couple_banner`→delete-old.
  - **UI:** a "Set couple photo" affordance on/over Item 9's hero (soft-gate-aware); `CoupleBanner` gains a photo layer that wins over the derived gradient when `effectiveBannerSource` resolves to `Photo`.
  - **Gate wiring:** new `Feature`/`PlanLimits` entry (`coupleBannerPhoto`, soft, shared, revert-to-derived) + a new row in the paywall **§8 feature map** ([subscription-paywall-design.md](subscription-paywall-design.md)).
  - **Does not change:** the dormant `users.avatar_url`, Leg 1's motif system, or Item 9's derived logic (Slice 2 wraps it, doesn't touch it).
- **Build order:** **Slice 2** — builds on Item 9's stable slot, its own commit; carries the paywall-doc updates.
- **Tier-1 tests (JVM):** `CoupleMapper` `bannerUrl` round-trip (Entity↔Dto↔Domain, null round-trips as null); `effectiveBannerSource(bannerUrl, unlocked)` → `Photo(url)` iff `unlocked && url != null`, else `Derived` (the load-bearing freeze/revert correctness).
- **Verify (at build):** verify-by-running on a paired staging couple — crop → compress → upload → `set_couple_banner` → banner renders; **partner sync** (A sets photo → pulls to B's identity card); **replace** deletes the old object; **lapse/flip** (enforcement ON → reverts to derived; re-grant → chosen photo auto-restores, no re-upload); **cleanup** (unpair + delete_account leave no readable orphan — DB/storage check). `testStagingDebugUnitTest` + `assembleStagingDebug` green.

## Item 13 — In-app "Connect Google account" (linkIdentity)

- **Status:** 📋 **PLANNED — GRILLED 2026-07-23 (Opus, medium effort), design locked ([ADR-0051](../adr/0051-in-app-connect-google-linkidentity.md)). Not yet built.** Model for the build: **Opus** (novel redirect/deep-link auth pathway; cross-ADR interactions with 0013/0021/0027). **Depends on [Item 2](#item-2--google-sign-in-pulled-from-post-v1-horizon-1) — but config-only, not code** (see Q7 below). **No schema/Room change** — a thin Settings surface onto `linkIdentity` + an identity read.
- **Request:** Alvin (during the Item 2 grill, 2026-07-23) — "if the user initially registered via email and password manually, do they get a chance to connect their Google account in their Ipon account?" Answer: not without this item. Decided to **split it out** of Item 2 as a separate follow-up rather than fold it in.
- **The distinction (why it's not already covered by Item 2):** Item 2's auto-linking (ADR-0050 decision 4) only links *implicitly* — an email user must **sign out**, then tap "Continue with Google" with a **matching** Gmail. This item is the *explicit, discoverable, stay-signed-in* path: a "Connect Google account" row in Settings (Profile → Account) that links Google to the account you're **already logged into**, and works even if the Google email **differs** from the registered one — the one thing auto-linking cannot do.
- **Grill outcome — load-bearing findings:** (1) **supabase-kt has no native ID-token link** — `linkIdentityWithIdToken` is JS/Dart-only; Kotlin has only `linkIdentity(Google)`, the **OAuth redirect (browser/Custom-Tab)** flow (the mechanism ADR-0050 rejected *for login*). Unavoidable. (2) **Manual linking is a Supabase beta feature, OFF by default** — must be enabled in the dashboard (`GOTRUE_SECURITY_MANUAL_LINKING_ENABLED`) or every link silently no-ops. (3) The redirect's outcome is **asynchronous** — `linkIdentity` returns as soon as it *launches* the browser; success/failure lands later via the `login-callback` deep link, so it can't be `try/catch`ed at the call site. Full rationale + rejected alternatives in **[ADR-0051](../adr/0051-in-app-connect-google-linkidentity.md)**.
- **Decisions (each a grilled fork):**
  1. **Different-email attach is the target (Q1)** — link a Google identity (possibly a different email) to the already-signed-in account; same-email convenience is a free side-benefit, not the justification. Copy says "Connect a Google account," not "so you can log in with Google."
  2. **Connect + status, no unlink (Q2)** — read the identity list → show Connected vs. Not-connected → offer Connect only when unlinked. **Unlink deferred** to a separate later item (its own risk surface: the only-identity lockout guard; Supabase enforces ≥2 identities server-side).
  3. **No new deep-link routing; outcome via resume-diff (Q3)** — a `linkIdentity` callback returns a normal same-user session (`type != "recovery"`), so `AuthRepositoryImpl.status` routes it to `Authenticated(sameUserId)`, never `PasswordRecovery`; same user id ⇒ no ADR-0021 account-switch purge. The existing `handleDeeplinks` absorbs it transparently. The Profile screen detects the result by **re-reading `currentIdentitiesOrNull()` on resume** (success = Google now present; cancel = unchanged, silent).
  4. **No Activity; reuse+widen the resume refresh (Q5)** — unlike Item 2's native flow, the redirect launches from the registered app context (no Activity plumbing). `AuthRepository` gains `linkGoogleIdentity()` (fire-and-launch) + `linkedGoogleIdentity(): LinkedIdentity?` (finds `provider == "google"` → `{ email }`), each behind a UseCase. `ProfileViewModel`'s existing per-resume `refreshEmail()` (which already calls `RefreshSessionUseCase` → `retrieveUserForCurrentSession(updateSession = true)`) is **widened** to also read the linked identity from the freshly-pulled session — post-link freshness solved for free.
  5. **Silent on cancel *and* completion-failure (Q6)** — redirect completion failures (**already linked to a different Ipon account**; **manual linking disabled**) arrive only in `handleDeeplinks`'s error callback, *not* at the call site, and via the resume-diff are **indistinguishable from a cancel**. Both degrade to a **silent no-op + a neutral "Google account wasn't connected." resume message** (not an alarming error) — safe because manual-linking-disabled is a config prereq we control and already-linked-elsewhere is rare + non-destructive. Launch-time failures → typed `AuthError.GOOGLE_LINK_FAILED`. Routing the specific completion error through is a noted **fast-follow** if testing shows the silent case confuses.
  6. **Always-show, state-driven row; show the linked Gmail (Q4/Q9)** — lives under the **Account** section of [ProfileScreen.kt](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/settings/presentation/ProfileScreen.kt) (~L164), grouped with Change password/email (above the error-colored Reset/Delete block). Not-linked → plain full-width `OutlinedButton` "Connect Google account" (**no Google "G" mark** — section consistency beats brand recognition here); linked → read-only "Google account" + connected Gmail + Connected affordance; a Google-signup user renders as the linked state. **No "set a password" affordance** for a Google-only user (inverse `updateUser { password }` feature — out of scope). Brief success confirmation on the flip.
  7. **Config-only coupling to Item 2; manual-linking is Item 13's own prereq (Q7)** — the redirect flow needs the Supabase Google provider + Web client + `login-callback` in the redirect allowlist (all *config* artifacts of ADR-0050, none of its *code* — no native `GoogleCredentialClient`/SHA-1 registration). So **no compile-time dependency on Item 2's code**; built after Item 2 only to inherit that dashboard setup. New own external prerequisite: **enable Manual Linking (beta flag)** in the dashboard. Staging-only.
- **External prerequisites (build depends on these — checklist):** (1) Item 2's Supabase Google provider config live (provider enabled, Web client ID set, `com.iponlove.app://login-callback` in the redirect allowlist — the last already present for recovery/email-confirm); (2) **Supabase dashboard → enable Manual Linking** (`GOTRUE_SECURITY_MANUAL_LINKING_ENABLED`) — a forgotten flag makes every link a silent no-op.
- **Tier-1 tests (JVM):** (1) the pure identity-resolution mapper (identity list → `LinkedIdentity?`: google present → its email, absent → null, google-without-email → `{ email = null }`); (2) launch-error → `AuthError.GOOGLE_LINK_FAILED` mapping. Rest is Android-heavy (browser/Custom-Tab/deep-link) → verify-by-running.
- **Does not change (this booking):** no code, schema, or Room change — stub only (grill/ADR + this booking update).
- **Verify (at build):** on-device (after Item 2 + the manual-linking flag are live) — an email user's Profile → Account shows "Connect Google account"; tapping opens the browser, completing with a Gmail lands back with the row flipped to "Connected · <gmail>"; a Google-signup user shows the connected state read-only; cancelling the browser shows the neutral "wasn't connected" message and no error; a Gmail already on another Ipon account degrades silently (fast-follow candidate). `testStagingDebugUnitTest` + `assembleStagingDebug` green.

## Item 14 — Orphaned receipt files are never cleaned up (device-storage leak)

- **Status:** ✅ **DONE `161acec`** (2026-07-24, Sonnet, low effort) — found during the [Item 6](#item-6--general-export-facility-csv--pdf--zip-receipt-photos-included) grill (Alvin's question: *"does the stray file get deleted, or am I paying for it in storage?"*). No grill needed. No schema/Room change. **Separate concern from Item 6** — deliberately not folded into the export slices.
- **The bug:** [CompressReceiptUseCase](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/domain/usecase/CompressReceiptUseCase.kt#L29) writes the compressed JPEG to `filesDir/receipts/{imageId}.jpg` **at pick time**, but the `transaction_images` row is only created on **Save**. Nothing ever deletes a file that never got a row. Grepped every `filesDir` use in the codebase: only two places write there (receipts, note attachments) and **nothing anywhere deletes an orphan** — the only cleanup that exists is in [TransactionImageUploader](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/data/upload/TransactionImageUploader.kt), which by definition only sees files that *have* a row.
- **Two ways to orphan a file, both live:**
  1. **Abandon the editor** after picking a receipt — file written, no row, stays forever.
  2. **Pick a receipt, then remove it before saving** — [AddTransactionViewModel.kt:245](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/presentation/AddTransactionViewModel.kt#L245)'s `onRemoveImage` drops the image from editor state and **does not touch the file**. This one leaks even on a successful save.
- **Blast radius:** ~150–300KB per orphan (1080px JPEG @85%), on the **user's device storage only** — never uploaded, so **no Supabase cost to us**. Invisible in Android's storage breakdown (generic app data); clearable only by uninstalling or "Clear storage" (which also destroys the login). Not urgent; genuinely wrong.
- **Notes are unaffected:** [AddNoteImageUseCase](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/notes/domain/usecase/AddNoteImageUseCase.kt) creates the `NoteAttachmentEntity` row **at pick time**, so the uploader always eventually owns the file. It is receipts' deferred row-creation that opens the gap.
- **Change — built as planned, two halves:** (1) [AddTransactionViewModel.kt](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/presentation/AddTransactionViewModel.kt)'s `onRemoveImage` now deletes the backing file when the image is still local (`localPath != null`, i.e. never uploaded) before dropping it from editor state; (2) a new `CleanupOrphanedReceiptsUseCase` sweeps `filesDir/receipts` on every app start (wired into `IponApp.onCreate` on the existing `appScope`, off the main thread), deleting any file whose id has no `transaction_images` row at all — deleted or not, uploaded or not. Backed by a new `TransactionImageRepository.allImageIds()` → `TransactionImageDao.allIds()` (`SELECT id FROM transaction_images`, no `isDeleted`/`url` filter, so a soft-deleted row pending upload still counts as "known" and is left alone). Half (2) alone fixes both leak paths; half (1) makes the common case immediate.
- **Does not change:** the upload path, the delete-after-upload behavior, `transaction_images` rows, or note attachments.
- **Tier-1 tests (JVM):** `CleanupOrphanedReceiptsUseCaseTest` — the orphan predicate extracted as a pure `orphanIds(diskIds, knownIds)` companion function: file with no row at all → orphan; row exists and is already uploaded → not an orphan; soft-deleted row pending upload → not an orphan (uploader owns it); mixed set flags only the unknown ids; empty disk set → no orphans. 5/5 green.
- **Verify:** `testStagingDebugUnitTest` + `assembleStagingDebug` both green. On-device verified by Alvin, alongside Item 12, before the joint commit.
